text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- An official delegation of the Republic of Tatarstan under the leadership of Vasilii Lichachov, chairman of the State Council of Tatarstan, will be visiting Latvia on August 18 - 20.
- Two state-owned buildings in the centre of Riga were sold at an auction for more than three million lats on August 15.

- During the first half of this year Latvia's key economic indicators improved, the finance ministry said. The price-adjusted gross domestic product was 695.7 million lats, an increase of 2.6% compared to 1996, and price-adjusted government revenues rose by 19.6 per-cent.

- In the first six months of this year Latvian exports reached 454.9 million lats, a 23 percent increase compared to the same period the previous year, and imports grew by 22.2 percent to 713.2 million lats.
- The criminal police and Interpol's local bureau are working on a priority system in the search for criminal suspects. They also want to make a list of "Latvia's most wanted."
- The state-owned gas utility Latvian Gas has been transformed into a public company.
